newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO raises forecast for end-97 cereal stocks.
newsitem.headline: FAO raises forecast for end-97 cereal stocks.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Monday it had raised its forecast for end-of-season cereal stocks for crop years ending in 1997 by some eight million tonnes to 285 million.
The Rome-based agency said in a special food outlook to coincide with a world food summit that the rise reflected prospects of larger than expected harvests in several countries.
"Assuming the forecast level of stocks materialises, this would be the first increase in four years, with carryovers rising by some 6.5 percent above their reduced opening level," the agency said.

However, it warned that the ratio of end-of-season carryovers in 1996/97 to trend utilisation in 1997/98 would still remain well below the range that FAO considered the minimum necessary to safeguard world food security.
Despite this year's increase in production, stocks were set to remain at 15.4 percent of annual consumption, below the FAO's safety threshold of 17-18 percent.
"Furthermore, all indications still point to a further erosion of stocks in developing countries, which are forecast to fall to their lowest level since 1991," it said.
